subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A fair six-sided die is rolled. What is P(rolling a 4)?
questions.explain: There is one favourable outcome out of six equally likely: 1/6.

questions.q: A fair coin is flipped twice. What is P(at least one head)?
questions.explain: P(at least one head) = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.q: Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.4 + 0.3 = 0.7.

questions.q: A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. What is P(red)?
A die is rolled 300 times and lands on 6 a total of 45 times. What is the experimental probability of a 6?
A coin is flipped 200 times and lands heads 90 times. What is the experimental probability of heads?
Two fair coins are flipped. What is P(both heads)?
The probability of winning a game is 0.2. In 50 games, how many wins are expected?
A bag has 4 red, 3 green and 1 yellow ball. What is P(green)?
In a tree diagram, the first branch shows P = 0.6 and a following branch shows P = 0.5. What is the probability of both happening?
In a Venn diagram, 5 people like tea only, 3 like coffee only and 2 like both, out of 12 people. How many like neither?
Two independent events have P(A) = 0.5 and P(B) = 0.4. What is P(A and B)?
questions.explain: For independent events P(A and B) = 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2.

questions.q: The probability a seed germinates is 0.8. Out of 250 seeds, how many are expected to germinate?
Probabilities for three outcomes are 0.2, 0.5 and x. What is x?
Which value could NOT be a probability?
questions.explain: Probabilities lie between 0 and 1, so 1.2 is impossible.

questions.q: Probabilities for four outcomes are 0.1, 0.25, 0.4 and x. What is x?
On the probability scale, what value represents an impossible event?
Events A and B are mutually exclusive with P(A) = 0.25 and P(B) = 0.45. What is P(A or B)?
questions.explain: For mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = 0.25 + 0.45 = 0.7.

questions.q: In a Venn diagram of 30 students, 12 study French only, 9 study Spanish only and 4 study both. How many study neither?
The probability it rains is 0.3. What is the probability it does not rain?
The probability a bus is late is 0.15. What is the probability it is not late?
A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is P(spinning an even number)?
questions.explain: There are 4 even numbers out of 8, so 4/8 = 1/2.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Mathematics (1MA1) specification; Probability
